Next, we present the sunflower lemma by Erdős and Rado [12] and a related definition of
sunflowers in set systems. In a set system (U, S), a sunflower F with z petals and core Y is a
collection of sets S1, . . . , Sz ∈S such that Si ∩Sj = Y for all i ̸= j. We refer to a set Si \ Y
as the petal corresponding to set Si and we require all petals to be non-empty. We state a
variant of it as proven in the textbook by Flum and Grohe [13, page 212].
▶Lemma 2.2 (Sunflower lemma). Let (U, S) be a set system, such that each set in S has
size at most d. If |S| > d · d!(z −1)d, then the set system contains a sunflower with z petals
and such a sunflower can be computed in time polynomial in |U|, |S|, and z.
The following lemma follows from the definitions of sunflowers and hitting sets.
▶Lemma 2.3 (⋆). Let (U, S) be a set system with sets of size ≤d for which there exists a
hitting set of size ≤h, for some integers d, h. Let X ⊆S be a collection of disjoint sets and
let F ⊆S be a sunflower of size d(h −1) + 2 that contains one of the sets X ∈X. Then,
there is a set X′ ∈F \ {X} such that (X \ X) ∪{X′} is a collection of pairwise disjoint sets.

## 1. Introduction

A family of at least three sets is a sunflower (or a Δ-system) if every element is contained either in all of the sets, or in at most one. If a family of sets contains no sets that form a sunflower, it is called sunflower-free. This notion was introduced by Erdős and Rado [10] in 1960, and it has become one of the standard tools in extremal combinatorics [14]. Erdős and Rado conjectured that the maximum size of any sunflower-free family of k-element sets is at most 𝑐𝑘, for a suitable constant 𝑐> 0. This conjecture is still open; for recent progress, see [4].

Erdős and Szemerédi [11] studied the maximum possible size of a sunflower-free family of subsets of {1,…,𝑛}. Denote this quantity by 𝑓⁡(𝑛) and let 𝜇= lim⁡𝑓⁡(𝑛)1/𝑛. Erdős and Szemerédi conjectured that 𝜇< 2, and this was proved by Naslund and Sawin [18], using the methods of Croot, Lev, P. Pach [6], Ellenberg and Gijswijt [8], and Tao [19]. They showed that 𝜇< 1.89, while the best currently known lower bound, 𝜇> 1.551, follows from a construction of Deuber et al. [7].
